t: Funds made available by this joint resolution shall be apportioned to the States in such manner as will best enable schools to meet their obligations with respect to the service of free and reduced price lunches and to meet the objective of this joint resolution with respect to providing a minimum rate of reimbursement under section 4 of the National School Lunch Act, and such funds shall be apportioned and paid as expeditiously as may be practicable.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mention of States and schools signals coordination with outside parties. But the section only directs how federal funds are apportioned and paid to States for school lunch reimbursement. It requires no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, so no outside party takes part in a federal decision.
fable.s: Funds made available by this joint resolution shall be apportioned to the States in such manner as will best enable schools to meet their obligations

qwen_block.w: This section describes the formula and timing for distributing federal funds to states. It does not require any consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as states, local governments, or the public) before the decision is made. The distribution is determined by statutory criteria ('in such manner as will best enable...'), not by a participatory process.
qwen_block.s: Funds made available by this joint resolution shall be apportioned to the States in such manner as will best enable schools to meet their obligations with respect to the service of free and reduced price lunches and to meet the objective of this joint resolution with respect to providing a minimum rate of reimbursement under section 4 of the National School Lunch Act, and such funds shall be apportioned and paid as expeditiously as may be practicable.

opus.w: This section only tells the federal government how to apportion and pay school-lunch funds to States. States and schools are named only as recipients of the money, not as parties consulted before a federal decision. Receiving funds is like a benefit or grant, which the definition excludes. The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.s: Funds made available by this joint resolution shall be apportioned to the States in such manner as will best enable schools to meet their obligations with respect to the service of free and reduced price lunches
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is "Yes" because States and schools, which are outside the federal government, are named. That fails the definition. The section only says how federal funds get apportioned and paid to States. Nobody outside the government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to object or sue. Receiving funds is like a benefit or grant, not taking part in the decision. No rulemaking authority is granted either.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates the apportionment of federal funds to states based on specific criteria (meeting school obligations and reimbursement rates). It does not require the federal government to consult with state or local officials, the public, or other outside entities before making the decision on how to distribute the funds. The states are passive recipients of the allocation, not active participants in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Funds made available by this joint resolution shall be apportioned to the States in such manner as will best enable schools to meet their obligations with respect to the service of free and reduced price lunches and to meet the objective of this joint resolution with respect to providing a minimum rate of reimbursement under section 4 of the National School Lunch Act, and such funds shall be apportioned and paid as expeditiously as may be practicable.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "apportioned to the States" implies coordination with state governments. However, the text describes a formulaic distribution of funds based on statutory objectives ("best enable schools to meet their obligations"), not a process of consultation or joint decision-making with state officials. The states are recipients of the funds, not participants in the decision of how to allocate them.
